Details.SubAgencyName: Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Office (SAPRO)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is located in the DoW Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Office (SAPRO). SAPRO reports to the Director, Defense Human Resources Activity (DHRA) and operationally is aligned under the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness. The SAPRO is responsible for the overall management, guidance, implementation of public laws, development of DoW policies, and policy oversight concerning sexual assault prevention and response matters within the War Department. The mission of the SAPRO is to enhance military readiness by eliminating sexual assaults. Responsibilities of the incumbent include serving as the single point of authority, accountable for oversight and providing authoritative leadership for the entire IPP portfolio that shapes a resilient and ready force by driving strategies that prevent readiness-distracting behaviors and foster strong command climates that value and respect all Service members, their families, and DoW civilians.
MajorDuties: As the Director, Force Readiness and Response (FRR)/ Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Office (SAPRO) the incumbent provides advice to senior leaders, oversight of a staff of senior professionals. Examples of major functions performed include: Serves as the subject matter expert and primary advisor on SAPR efforts. This includes policy formulation, oversight, management and integration of all established goals across the DoW. These programs are extremely complex and require expert knowledge of the full range of laws, policies, and programs necessary to prevent sexual assault and institute evidence based primary prevention efforts for all eligible populations. The incumbent is responsible for the standards, directives, and instructions governing the execution of the programs in this area. Serves as the lead prevention officer, program manager, and policy advisor for all prevention issues. This includes the oversight, management, and integration of all primary prevention matters to ensure coordination and conformity of execution with established goals. The incumbent provides advice and assistance on a broad range of analytical research, legislation, and policy related to the Integrated Primary Prevention (IPP) mission and also develops, coordinates, reviews, and evaluates IPP programs, plans, and special projects. They develop and oversee policies, regulations, and communication tools that have agency-wide usage and directly affect the prevention of harmful behaviors across the Military Departments, DoW Agencies, Field Activities, and Combatant Commands. Provides oversight and management of all policy administration and program formulation/execution within the FRR. The incumbent is responsible for the execution and has full managerial authority for organizing and directing all activities across the FRR and has the full range of supervisory responsibilities necessary for functional oversight and administrative and fiscal management. Represents DoW in contacts with appropriate segments of the Legislative, Executive, and Judicial Branches of the Federal Government; professional, special interest, and public citizens groups; and the media (in coordination with the Office of the Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs (OATSW(PA)) staff) on prevention and response matters. Maintains liaison and direct day-to-day relationships with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM), OMB, Government Accountability Office (GAO), Committees of both Houses of Congress in coordination with the Assistant Secretary of War for Legislative Affairs (ASW(LA)) staff, professional associations, and supervisory organizations. Works closely with top-level representatives of the Military Departments and DoW Agencies and the offices of other Deputy Assistant Secretaries of War. Represents DoW on various inter-governmental boards and committees. Establishes and directs the effort of high-level DoW-wide working groups, gains the cooperation of the Military Services and DoW Components, and gains the support of outside organizations such as OPM, OMB, GAO, the White House, and Congress. Oversees operation of the SAPR Training and Education Center of Excellence and employs this operation to establish core competencies and oversee the effectiveness of SAPR and primary prevention program training and the sharing of best practices to comprehensively address stakeholders' requirements for SAPR, IPP, and oversight activities across the DoW. Develops requirements and oversees operation of the DoW Safe Helpline, the Department's crisis support activity for members of the military community impacted by sexual assault. The incumbent follows established procedures for contracting, cybersecurity, authority to operate, and other matters to ensure that the Safe Helpline stays available around the clock throughout the world.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Department of War, Defense Security Cooperation Agency. This is a Tier III SES level position.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: DSCA's mission is to advance U.S. national security and foreign policy interests by building the capacity of foreign security forces to respond to shared challenges. DSCA leads the broader U.S. security cooperation enterprise in its efforts to train, educate, advise, and equip foreign partners. DSCA administers security cooperation programs that support U.S. policy interests and objectives.
MajorDuties: This position is part of the Department of War, Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA). DSCA is responsible for planning, coordinating, administering, and supervising Department of War (DOW) programs for transfer of defense articles, services, and technology, by sale or grant to foreign governments and international organizations. These programs include Foreign Military Sales (FMS) under which defense articles and services are sold to foreign countries or international organizations, Foreign Military Financing (FMF) under which grants or loans are provided to foreign countries for financing of FMS or direct commercial contracts with U.S. industry, International Military Education and Training (IMET) under which financial assistance is provided to foreign students attending U.S. military schools, and Humanitarian Assistance and Demining (HAID) and Overseas Humanitarian Disaster and Civic Aid (OHDACA), as well as other Title 10 security cooperation authorities (section 332 and 333 authorities), under which support is provided to foreign governments.. DUTIES: In accordance with US Code, Title 10, Section 382, is responsible for the execution and administration of all security cooperation programs and activities of the DoW involving the provision of defense articles, military training, and other defense-related services by grant, loan, cash sale, or lease. Directs, administers, and provides DoW-wide security cooperation administration and execution guidance. Plans, manages, and directs DSCA, its subordinate elements, and all assigned resources, including by setting organization goals and priorities, allocating organizational resources, and managing internal relationships. Oversees and exercises overall management responsibility for the Defense Security Cooperation University (DSCU), which provides consolidated Security Cooperation training and education for the Security Cooperation Workforce and the broader Security Cooperation enterprise. Represents the interests of the Secretary of War and the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (USW(A&S)) in security cooperation matters. Manages the Defense Security Cooperation Service (DSCS), which manages the manning, training, and administrative support for military and civilian Security Cooperation Offices around the world.

This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.SubAgencyName: U.S. Army Combat and Capabilities Development Command
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES) which is a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Department of the Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
MajorDuties: The Extramural Research Office (ERO) serves under the supervision of the Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (FASCOM), Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM), Army Research Laboratory (ARL) Director. The DEVCOM ARL is responsible for providing guidance in terms of broadly defined Army, T2COM, DEVCOM & ARL policies, mission and functions. To include a workforce of approximately 91 civilians professional, scientific, administrative, technical, and support personnel including 2 STs and 4 DB-Vs; 1 military; and approximately 21 contract personnel. Civilian S&T workforce consists of DB-02/03/04 (GS07-15 equivalent), primarily at the DB-03 level. Serves as the Director, Extramural Research Office. Responsible for setting and executing the nationwide extramural research agenda and programs on Army focused basic research within the biological and biotechnology; electromagnetic spectrum; energy; information; humans in complex systems; mechanical; network, cyber, & computational; photonics, electronics & quantum; extreme materials; terminal effects; and weapons sciences to provide critical enhancements to current warfighter needs and revolutionary advances required for technological dominance of the future force with emphasis on the Army's Modernization Priorities. Manages an annual Army Research Office (ARO) budget exceeding $253M in order to provide full life cycle management from topic formulation through scientific and fiscal program execution. Manages technology transition initiation for more than 1,700 grants and contracts performed by approximately 3,500 researchers at approximately 300 universities and businesses. Responsible for oversight of the entire ARL extramural 6.1 program. Serves as a member of high-level executive scientific and technology committees and groups at the international, national, Office of the Secretary of War, Department of the Army, and other Federal Agency levels, providing technical expertise and influencing executive- level policy and programs. Exercises line authority and technical direction over the total office program. Acquisition Position Information: 1. This is a Critical Acquisition Position (CAP). Practitioner Career Level Certification Category must be met within 5 years.

Complete a Declaration for Federal Employment to determine your suitability for Federal employment, at the time requested by the agency If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System or are exempt from having to do so. You must be able to submit and pass designated and/or Random Drug Testing as required. File a Confidential Financial Disclosure Report OGE-278e within 30 days of appointment and annually from then on. Appointment is subject to the completion of a favorable suitability or fitness determination, as determined by a background investigation. You must be able to obtain/maintain the appropriate clearance and access level for this position. Failure to obtain and maintain the required level of clearance may result in the withdrawal of a job offer or removal. Direct deposit of pay is required. The incumbent is required to travel on both scheduled and unscheduled aircraft, and other modes as required, under conditions specified under the DoD Joint Travel Regulations. The incumbent is expected to travel on short notice to attend high level meetings to obtain resolution of problems and gather information to assist in the decision-making process. Mobility: An essential element of the SES is mobility across geographic, organizational and functional lines. Individuals selected for Army SES positions may be subject to reassignment that requires them to be mobile. You must sign a mobility agreement. There are three key documents that contain important information about your rights and obligations. Please read and retain these documents: Noncriminal Justice Applicant's Privacy Rights, for those who undergo an FBI fingerprint-based criminal history record check for personnel vetting, which includes Rap Back, FD-258 Privacy Act Statement - FBI (this is the same statement used when your fingerprints are submitted as part of your background investigation), and SEAD-3-Reporting-U.pdf (dni.gov), (applicable to those who hold a sensitive position or have eligibility for access to classified information).
Details.Evaluations: You will be evaluated for this job based on how well you meet the qualifications above. Once the application process is complete, a review of your resume and supporting documentation will be conducted. If you meet minimum qualifications, your Application Package will be further reviewed to determine if you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualification (MTQ) listed above. ECQs and TQ must be thoroughly addressed within your two (2) page resume. Separate narratives will not be accepted or reviewed. Highly Qualified applicants may undergo one or more interviews and may be referred to the selecting official for further consideration. Upon selection, if not already a member of the SES serving under a career appointment, the individual selected must have his/her executive qualifications certified by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB) before appointment to this position. The selected individual's application will be forwarded to the OPM for review and certification by the QRB, unless the selectee provides evidence of their noncompetitive status (i.e., a current SES, OPM QRB certified SESCDP graduate, or SES reinstatement eligible). Upon QRB certification, the selected individual will be required to serve a one-year probationary period. For more information regarding the SES, go to https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/senior-executive-service/.

Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATION (TQ): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the following technical qualification. TQ: Ability to develop, implement, and coordinate comprehensive programs in the areas of Records Management, Freedom of Information Act, printing and publishing, and 508 compliance programs. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQ, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES) which is a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Department of the Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
MajorDuties: The Executive Director, Enterprise Services Agency leads a Field Operating Agency of the Office of the Administrative Assistant to the Secretary of the Army to provide products and services in support of the Army, other military departments, the Joint Staff, Office of the Secretary of War, and other federal agencies for the Pentagon community. Manages shared administrative, information technology, and operational products and services for Department of the Army headquarters. Exercises responsibility for Army Enterprise Service and support missions related to Records Management, Freedom of Information Act, Army Publishing, and the Army 508 program. Exercises full responsibility for the development, implementation, and coordination of comprehensive programs in the areas of Records Management, Freedom of Information Act services, Privacy and Civil Liberties, Document Declassification, Army Publications and Forms Management, NATO Central U.S. Registry Inspections, and Army 508 program. Oversees the provisioning of common enterprise-level information technology, administrative, and operational support products to the Army, other military departments, and defense agencies. Manages localized and shared infrastructure, customer service frameworks, and operational capabilities dedicated to the headquarters and National Capital Region personnel. With an annual budget of $275.7 million, incumbent exercises strategic management and oversight of 175 personnel to include 6 direct reporting personnel responsible for a multitude of enterprise level services for organizations Army-wide.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has training, education and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. In accordance with the new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs) when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practice. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board. To meet minimum qualifications requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the education, Technical Qualifications (TQ) and Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for this position. CERTIFICATION: This position will require DAWIA APDP Level III Certification in any acquisition profession career field and member of Acquisition Corps that must be obtained within 4 years of of encumbering this position. TQ1: Demonstrated ability to lead a large, globally dispersed, and functionally diverse services acquisition organization. The ideal candidate must describe their experience overseeing a complex portfolio of programs comparable in scope to AMIC's $22B portfolio, which supports worldwide operations. This includes experience managing the integration of multiple acquisition and support functions (e.g., Program Management, Contracting, Engineering, Logistics, Finance, and Legal) to deliver mission-critical capabilities. Candidates should provide specific examples of how they have allocated resources, managed personnel, and ensured effective execution to support the strategic objectives of a major command or agency. TQ2: Demonstrated ability to develop and implement a strategic vision to transform acquisition processes for enhanced speed, agility, and lethality. The ideal candidate must describe their experience in challenging the status quo by introducing innovative acquisition strategies, such as commercial solutions openings and outcome-based contracting, to meet urgent warfighter needs. This includes providing specific examples of leading organizational change, fostering a culture of innovation and informed risk-taking, and effectively engaging with senior leaders across the Department of War, other government agencies, and the industrial base to shape policy and align enterprise acquisition efforts with the National Defense Strategy. IDEAL CANDIDATE: The ideal candidate for the Director of ACC AMIC must be an elite, visionary acquisition executive possessing a minimum of 10 years of senior-level acquisition experience, including at least 4 years in a Critical Acquisition Position and a mandatory DAWIA Level III (or professional equivalent) certification in Contracting or Program Management. A candidate with strong Contracting background is preferred as the position requires significant depth in contracting rules, regulations (i.e., the new Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations), and best practices to oversee the implementation and execution of innovative acquisition strategies, complex source selections and source selection teams, and post-award contract management. The best candidate will possess a proven track record of leading complex, multi-functional organizations, and a demonstrated mastery of managing multi-billion-dollar acquisition portfolios, specifically focusing on large-scale services acquisitions, program management, strategic sourcing, and global operational program execution. To succeed in this high-impact role the candidate must have a deep understanding of the entire acquisition lifecycle from requirements generation to contract execution. Furthermore, they must be an innovative and agile leader capable of securing critical resources and driving cultural and procedural transformation, alongside a history of directing and developing highly diverse, multi-disciplinary teams of military, civilian, and contractor personnel. Crucially, the candidate must possess the political acumen and strategic communication skills required to represent the command at the highest echelons of the Department of War, Headquarters Air Force, and the Defense Industrial Base. Ultimately, the selected leader will be a transformative agent change who champions innovative, agile acquisition pathways and outcome-based contracting strategies to rapidly deliver lethal capabilities directly to the joint warfighter. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. SALARY: $151,661.00 - $209,600.00 per annum. (Air Force Tier 1) SES members are eligible for bonuses and/or ranks and stipends in addition to annual salary. AREA OF CONSIDERATION: Applications will be accepted from all qualified persons. SES members are eligible for Performance-Based Salary increases and/or bonuses. This is a SES Career Reserved position and is assigned a precedence priority code of DV-6/ Brig Gen, Tier 1 for protocol purposes. MOBILITY: Organizational and geographical mobility is essential in developing and managing SES and DISES leaders and generally is a key to advancement. Therefore, mobility is a condition of employment and appointed SES and DISES members will be required to sign a Reassignment Rights and Obligation Agreement.
MajorDuties: The Director of the Air Combat Command Acquisition Management and Integration Center (ACC AMIC) leads a highly complex, globally dispersed services acquisition enterprise with a multi-billion-dollar portfolio supporting critical, worldwide warfighting operations across three Combatant Commands. In this capacity, the Director is responsible for the strategic planning, policy formulation, and execution of a $22 billion acquisition portfolio, which includes high-visibility programs like MQ-9 operations, Contract Adversary Air Support (AdAir), and international counternarcotics initiatives spanning 210 countries. The incumbent secures vital financial, manpower, and material resources to maintain readiness across all detachments and operating locations. Additionally, the Director exercises direct managerial control over a diverse, multi-disciplinary team of 535 military, civilian, and contractor personnel, actively fostering their professional development. Finally, the Director serves as the primary Air Combat Command representative in high-level Secretary of the Air Force (SAF), Headquarters Air Force (HAF), and cross-MAJCOM forums, ensuring strategic alignment and advocate-level representation for the command's acquisition and sourcing requirements.

An applicant's resume must show that their experience, education and accomplishments reflect the competence and professional standing required to provide expertise needed for this position. INTELLIGENCE COMMUNITY SENIOR OFFICER CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ICSOCQ) Leading the Intelligence Enterprise. This core qualification involves the ability to integrate resources, information, interests, and activities effectively in support of the Intelligence Community's (IC) mission and to lead and leverage cross-organizational collaborative networks to achieve significant mission results. Inherent to this senior officer qualification is a deep understanding of the Intelligence enterprise and a shared commitment to the IC's core values. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs) TQ 1. Executive/expert level experience leading a large, complex operations or production unit., including programming, budgeting and resourcing. TQ 2. Demonstrated change management skills focused on introducing new technology to achieve greater mission outcomes. TQ 3. Broad understanding of international (e.g., International Hydrographic Organization), Inter-Agency, Inter-Governmental Organizations (IGO), Non-Governmental Organizations (NGO), multi-lateral and bi-lateral arrangements directly related or similar to those impacting maritime safety of navigation (SoN) processes. TQ 4. Broad understanding of the DoD and civil (e.g. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration) maritime community and its associated organizations, policies and programs. TQ 5. Demonstrated knowledge of the technical requirements, capabilities and challenges related to mapping, charting and digital navigation. EDUCATION REQUIREMENT Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. DESIRABLE QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: In addition to the mandatory qualifications, experience in the following is desired: 1. Experience in a maritime related field (cartography, bathymetry, maritime analysis, maritime navigation) 2. Knowledge of current and future DoD maritime navigation requirements. 3. Expert level knowledge regarding production of maritime related products and data.

MajorDuties: The Deputy Director, Maritime Safety Office (DD/SFH) is accountable for the development, sustainment, accuracy, and currency of a global maritime Safety of Navigation (SoN) product portfolio used to support navigation aboard all Department of War (DoW) surface and subsurface naval vessels. The DD/SFH develops and executes strategy to achieve long-term mission outcomes within the constraints of U.S. Code, international treaties, and applicable standards, and ensures alignment with NGA strategic objectives and mission imperatives. The DD/SFH maintains a deep understanding of the producer-mariner relationship and advances effective user engagement by interfacing with senior military leaders across the Services, FVEY and other international partners, and key multinational organizations including the International Hydrographic Organization (IHO) and NATO. The DD/SFH supports global readiness by assessing user needs; evaluating product availability, production timelines, and distribution pathways; and recommending strategies to optimize dissemination and operational utility. The DD/SFH works across the DoW, Intelligence Community (IC), and international partnerships to drive modernization of maritime SoN capabilities, with emphasis on implementing the S-100 Universal Hydrographic Framework. The DD/SFH leads and coordinates modernization initiatives that introduce new data sources, technologies, and production processes to improve quality, increase throughput, and strengthen resiliency of SoN production. The DD/SFH engages senior intelligence, defense, national, and international stakeholders on matters of national and international interest to share data, information, and tradecraft; establish collaborative practices; and shape doctrine, operating concepts, and business models impacting the GEOINT enterprise across the IC and DoW. The DD/SFH represents the IC and DoW in national and international forums to advance data sharing, cost/burden sharing, and cooperative production arrangements supporting next-generation Foundation GEOINT services. The DD/SFH oversees the quality, accuracy, and timeliness of geospatial information produced in-house, via contractors, and through national and international co-producers in support of military, civil, and allied partners. The DD/SFH provides leadership and oversight for SFH strategic integration and modernization, and maintains broad knowledge of maritime products and data, including the systems and workflows supporting in-house production, co-production, commodity sourcing, and contract-based data extraction, analysis, and finishing. As a member of the Source executive leadership team, the DD/SFH contributes to enterprise modernization efforts aligned to agency, component, and group-level Strategic Objectives, including data sharing and integration, collection, workforce development, and dissemination across the Source enterprise, supporting a modern, outcome-driven organization. The DD/SFH translates organizational priorities into executable programs and is accountable for office performance through direct management and oversight of division chiefs and senior staff. The incumbent leads a workforce of approximately 400 personnel (federal civilian, military, and contractor) located across NGA-Washington, NGA-St. Louis, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), and overseas locations. The DD/SFH plans, defends, and executes a multi-million-dollar annual budget through the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process; adjusts objectives, work plans, schedules, and resource allocations as needed; and exercises sound judgment in managing Source enterprise-level contracts supporting maritime SoN requirements. The DD/SFH supports the Director, SFH in representing the Director, Source Operations and Management Directorate as the SoN mission manager, and the Director, NGA in the SoN functional management role. The DD/SFH partners closely with the SoN Senior GEOINT Advisor (SGA) and the Maritime SGA to execute and oversee the maritime SoN mission.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has education, training, and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. In accordance with new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs), when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practices. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board (QRB). To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the education, Technical Qualifications (TQ), and Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ1. Constitutional Literacy, Democratic Oversight, Civic Trust, Treaty/Statutory Compliance. Directs the development and legal review of all operational plans (OPLANs) to include nuclear employment concepts. Ensures that all plans conform strictly to Title 10 (Armed Forces) and Title 50 (War and National Defense) of the U.S. Code, international humanitarian law, and standing arms control treaties. Establishes and maintains transparent, authoritative channels of communication with congressional committees, the White House, and defense oversight bodies. Translates highly classified operational capabilities and requirements into clear, unclassified and classified briefings that support legislative oversight and safeguard the public trust. TQ2. Strategic Integration, Interagency Diplomacy, Portfolio Synchronization, Outcome Delivery. Acts as the primary "senior diplomat" for USSTRATCOM strategy, policy, and plans issues in Washington, D.C., representing the command's strategic equities with fierce diplomacy in high-stakes forums. Routinely briefs, advises, and negotiates policy and resource allocations with 4-Star General Officers, the Secretary and Undersecretaries of War/Defense, the Joint Staff Operations Deputies (OpsDeps), and White House National Security Council staff. Leverages collaborative executive authority to dismantle institutional barriers between Combatant Commands (CCMDs). Leads cross-functional, inter-organizational working groups to synchronize USSTRATCOM's global deterrence posture with the geographic and functional operations of partner commands, producing integrated, multi-domain options for the President. Deploys a mature, pre-existing network of high-level contacts across the Joint Staff, the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW)/Defense, the Department of Energy (DOE), the Department of State, and the Intelligence Community. Mobilizes this network to rapidly resolve coordination deadlocks and build consensus during fast-breaking strategic crises. Delivers highly integrated, timely, and credible strategic options to the President. Ensures these options combine kinetic and non-kinetic capabilities, are thoroughly vetted against adversary perceptions and force availability, and directly preserve presidential decision space during national security emergencies. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): All new appointees to the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the five mandatory ECQs: ECQ 1. Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding: Demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2. Driving Efficiency: Demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3. Merit and Competence: Demonstrated knowledge, ability, and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Please note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program, or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50 or Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.JobSummary: As the Deputy Director for Plans and Policy (DJ5) at USSTRATCOM, you serve as the senior civilian executive leading global strategic deterrence during a complex shift to a multi-polar nuclear landscape. Working with the J5 Director, you oversee day-to-day operations and a diverse workforce. Your mission is dual-track: sustaining legacy systems while rapidly modernizing capabilities across cyber and space, acting as a key diplomat to OSW/OSD and the NSC.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Develop Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: The Deputy Director for Plans and Policy (DJ5) at USSTRATCOM is the senior civilian executive responsible for ensuring that all strategic operational plans and nuclear employment concepts strictly align with Title 10 and Title 50 of the U.S. Code, international law, and arms control treaties. To maintain democratic oversight and safeguard public trust, the Deputy Director establishes transparent communication channels with congressional committees, the White House, and defense oversight bodies, translating highly classified capabilities into clear briefings. As the primary champion for human-in-the-loop systems integrity, the incumbent systematically audits artificial intelligence and machine learning integrations within warning systems to protect presidential decision-making authority. Operational efficiency is driven through calculated risk management, balancing the fail-safe sustainment of legacy platforms with the rapid scaling of modernized kinetic and non-kinetic capabilities. The Deputy Director exercises direct executive control over an operational budget of up to $9.2 million-including key portfolios like Deterrence Assurance Planning Support ($1.6M-$1.8M) and Tri-lab funding ($2.7M-$3.1M)-by streamlining contract integration and holding contractors to performance-based benchmarks. Efficiency is further enhanced by adopting advanced software, big data analytics, and cloud tools to automate routine administrative workflows, freeing human intelligence for high-priority strategic analysis. This role demands elite cognitive agility to transition between zero-defect nuclear operations and the agile thinking required to navigate space, cyber, and electromagnetic spectrum domains. Serving as the chief futurist, the Deputy Director leads long-range intelligence-fusion efforts to anticipate adversary technological breakthroughs, such as hypersonics and quantum communications, and preemptively adjusts USSTRATCOM's strategic posture. Applying authoritative technical expertise in Joint doctrine and nuclear command and control, the incumbent designs unified plans integrating conventional, nuclear, and non-kinetic options. Leading a highly specialized joint workforce of approximately 190 active military, 205 federal civilians, and 37 contractor personnel, the Deputy Director builds a collaborative culture of innovation and psychological safety where personnel can challenge outdated processes without reprisal. This leadership actively supports physical, mental, and professional resilience while cultivating future national security leaders through dedicated mentorship and succession planning for the Senior Executive Service and flag-officer ranks. To achieve critical results, the Deputy Director acts as USSTRATCOM's primary senior diplomat in Washington, D.C., negotiating policy and resource allocations with 4-star generals, the Secretary of War/Defense, the Joint Staff, and the National Security Council. The incumbent dismantles institutional silos between Combatant Commands by leading cross-functional working groups to synchronize global deterrence postures. By leveraging a mature, pre-existing network across the Joint Staff, OSW/OSD, the Department of Energy, the Department of State, and the Intelligence Community, the Deputy Director rapidly resolves coordination deadlocks during fast-breaking crises. Ultimately, these efforts deliver highly integrated, timely, and credible strategic options to the President, combining kinetic and non-kinetic capabilities to preserve vital presidential decision space during national security emergencies.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES) which is a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. MajorDuties: Serves as the principal Deputy to the G-4 Director for Materiel Management, exercising delegated executive leadership, technical authority, and policy oversight for the Department of Army's enterprise materiel management portfolio on the Army Staff. The incumbent directly influences global combat readiness by shaping strategic plans and adapting Army policy across field and sustainment maintenance operations, enterprise supply processes, and troop support services (to include munitions, medical logistics, individual clothing and equipment, mortuary affairs, and food service operations). During the Program Objective Memorandum (POM) build, the Deputy Director acts as a key advisor in the Army's centralized programming processes, coordinating with stakeholders across all Army components to collect, validate, and prioritize multi-billion dollar O&MA requirements. Additionally, the Deputy Director drives enterprise-wide logistics IT modernization by partnering with ASA(ALT), T2COM, AMC, and CASCOM to establish functional requirements for next-generation ERPs and predictive analytics. Finally, the incumbent advises on strategic talent management, recruitment, and career development for thousands of professional civilian careerists in the Logistics Career Field.

TQ 2: Demonstrated ability to architect and institutionalize enterprise-wide transformations of financial management systems and processes, establishing systemic policy reforms and financial controls that integrate acquisition, technology, and fiscal structures to drive modernization across a global, complex organization. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. Sub-Competencies: Knowledge of the American System of Government: Demonstrates understanding and appreciation of the American system of government, including the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, separation of powers, federalism, and the historical development of the American Nation. Commitment to the Rule of Law: Upholds the principles of the American Founding, including equality under the law and democratic self-government. Ensures the law is applied fairly and consistently. Civic-Mindedness: Stays up-to-date on important developments in American government and aligns organizational objectives and practices with presidential and public interests. Demonstrates a commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. Sub-Competencies: Fiscal Responsibility: Strategically manages, allocates and monitors financial resources. Aligns priorities and initiatives to justify budget proposals. Monitors expenditures, cuts unnecessary costs, and uses cost-benefit analysis to set priorities. Managing Resources: Manages resources efficiently and effectively based on current and projected organizational goals, skills, budget considerations, and staffing needs. Leveraging Technology: Explores emerging technology and potential applications. Incorporates technology to enhance efficiency and achieve results. Ensures access to and security of technology systems. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. Sub-Competencies: Technical Skill: Possesses the requisite technical knowledge and subject matter expertise to consistently produce timely, high-quality work. Is considered a strong contributor in his or her domain. Problem Solving: Engages in critical and data-driven thinking when diagnosing root causes and evaluating options. Identifies and promptly addresses the most pressing, high-priority problems. Agility and Resilience: Anticipates and adapts to change, new ideas, new information, and new conditions. Is committed to continuous improvement. Deals effectively with pressure and remains optimistic and persistent, even under adversity. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. Sub-Competencies: Accountability: Ensures that employees are appropriately recruited, selected, appraised, trained, and retained. Takes swift action to address performance- or conduct-based deficiencies in employees supervised. Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Developing Others: Recognizes and rewards outstanding achievement in others. Develops the ability of others to perform and contribute to the organization by providing opportunities to learn through formal and informal methods. Cultivates a dynamic environment in which employees are not afraid to make mistakes. Executive Judgement: Makes well-reasoned, timely, and effective decisions and considers short- and long-term implications. Communicates effectively with stakeholders across all organizational levels, sharing and guarding information where appropriate. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Sub-Competencies: Operational Mindset: Effectively translates strategies into actionable steps and processes. Partners effectively with stakeholders to drive adoption and addresses blockers to ensure successful implementation. Innovation: Applies creativity to improving products and processes, challenges convention, takes measured risks, and considers ways to simplify and remove unnecessary requirements. Strategic Thinking: Formulates objectives and priorities and implements plans consistent with the long-term interests of the organization by evaluating conditions, resources, capabilities, constraints, and organizational goals and values. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has training, education and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. In accordance with the new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs) when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practice. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board. To meet minimum qualifications requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the education, Technical Qualifications (TQ) and Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for this position. CERTIFICATIONS: The incumbent must possess or be willing to obtain Cybersecurity Workforce Management certification (8570.01 IAM level III) or equivalent within one year of gaining the position. TQ1: Enterprise Cybersecurity Strategy, Governance, and Risk Management Demonstrated senior executive experience leading enterprise-wide cybersecurity strategy, governance, and risk management within a large, complex organization. This includes establishing cybersecurity policies, standards, and accountability frameworks; aligning security investments and priorities with organizational mission objectives; and advising senior executives on enterprise cyber risk, risk acceptance, and resource allocation. Proven ability to influence enterprise decisions, drive organizational change, and establish measurable improvements in cybersecurity posture and resilience. TQ2: Cybersecurity Operations, Enterprise Risk Reduction, and Mission Resilience Demonstrated senior executive experience overseeing complex cybersecurity programs and operations to protect mission-critical systems, networks, data, and services. This includes directing enterprise cyber defense, vulnerability and exposure management, incident response, and security modernization initiatives; integrating cybersecurity into enterprise technology architectures and operations; and translating threat intelligence and operational risk into prioritized action. Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary organizations, establish clear accountability, and deliver measurable risk reduction and operational resilience across a distributed enterprise. TQ3: Executive Leadership and Enterprise Transformation Demonstrated senior executive experience leading large, multidisciplinary organizations through complex cybersecurity transformation. This includes aligning organizational structures, authorities, resources, and performance measures to enterprise priorities; influencing senior stakeholders across organizational boundaries; and overcoming institutional barriers to deliver measurable outcomes. Proven ability to establish accountability, develop executive talent, and lead sustained organizational change. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): All new appointees to the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the five mandatory ECQs: ECQ 1. Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding:Demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2. Driving Efficiency:Demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3. Merit and Competence: Demonstrated knowledge, ability, and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4. Leading People:Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results:Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Please note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program, or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50 or Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. SALARY: $151,662.00 - $219,000.00 per annum. (Air Force Tier 1) SES members are eligible for bonuses and/or ranks and stipends in addition to annual salary. AREA OF CONSIDERATION: Applications will be accepted from all qualified persons. SES members are eligible for Performance-Based Salary increases and/or bonuses. This is a SES Career Reserved position and is assigned a precedence priority code of DV-6/ Brig Gen, Tier 1 for protocol purposes. MOBILITY: Organizational and geographical mobility is essential in developing and managing SES and DISES leaders and generally is a key to advancement. Therefore, mobility is a condition of employment and appointed SES and DISES members will be required to sign a Reassignment Rights and Obligation Agreement.
MajorDuties: As the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) for the Department of the Air Force, you will serve as a key executive leader directing the cybersecurity strategy and cyber defense programs across the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force. In this high-impact role, you will advise senior leaders, shape enterprise-wide cybersecurity policies, and ensure the resilience of global operations and systems against emerging cyber threats. You will: Direct and manage a comprehensive, DAF-wide cybersecurity program to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of all supporting information systems. Establish and oversee policies and procedures based on the DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) to consistently identify, assess and mitigate information security risks. Serve as the DAF Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP) and the Senior Agency Official for Records Managemenbt (SAORM). Lead the development, validation and prioritization of Cyberspace Operational capability requirements and doctrine. Direct enterprise security awareness and training programs for all personnel and contractors, alongside periodic testing of security controls. Establish processes to detect, report and swiftly respond to cybersecurity incidents and rectify any identified policy or practice deficiencies. Engage in real-time cyber defense operations and cyber command and control (C2) to integrate global effects. Collaborate with executive-level experts, Defense Industrial Base representatives, and academia to identify strategic gaps and leverage emerging cybersecurity technologies. Advise senior leaders (including DoD, Joint Staff and Combatant Commands) on current cybersecurity trends, metrics and cyber defense planning. Provide executive supervision, guidance and leadership for four divisions comprising military, civilian and contractor personnel.
Details.Education: Education: A Bachelor's or Master's Degree in an Information Technology related field (e.g., Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Data Science or Information Systems) is desired. Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) and/or Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) certification is highly desired. In addition, DoW requires an Enterprise Perspective. The individual must possess a broad point of view and an awareness and understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to DoW or government-wide strategic priorities. Executives must demonstrate an ability to work with internal and external partners to support national security objectives. This perspective is typically gained through a variety of diverse work experiences. This information should be embedded within the resume.

This authority allows us to appoint qualified individuals to initial career appointments into the Senior Executive Service of the DoD without regard to 5 U.S.C. 3393(c). Details.JobSummary: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is a separate Agency of the Department of War (DoW) under the direction, authority, and control of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (USW (I&S)). This position is placed in the Personnel Vetting (PV) Trust Decision office and reports to DCSA's Deputy Associate Director, Trust Decision. This is a Tier 1 position.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our MissionThrough vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our VisionDCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution PlanThe Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. To learn more about DCSA's mission and vision, visit: https://www.dcsa.mil/About-Us/Careers/
MajorDuties: The Technical Director, Trust Decision (Adjudications) serves as the principal advisor to senior management on how best to assure the development, integration, and continuous improvement of key adjudicative frameworks. Specifically, the incumbent oversees the policies, analytic methods, quality-assurance practices, workforce capabilities, and enabling technologies essential to making and supporting sound trust determinations. They exercise delegated final authority for assigned enterprise adjudication functions. Responsibilities Include: Serves as the principal advisor and authoritative technical authority to senior leadership on complex adjudicative matters, policy interpretation, emerging risks, and legislative changes; renders final technical determinations and provides decision-quality briefings, executive correspondence, and strategic recommendations to guide enterprise priorities. Leads the development, refinement, and execution of enterprise trust-determination strategies, policy proposals, and governance mechanisms; establishes operational approaches and technical frameworks that ensure risk-based, fair, consistent, and legally defensible adjudicative decisions. Directs strategic oversight for enterprise adjudication operations by establishing robust quality-management frameworks, internal controls, and case-review methodologies; analyzes workload drivers and performance indicators to resolve systemic issues and drive continuous business process improvement. Represents the Agency in high-level engagements with Department of War Components, Federal agencies, the Intelligence Community, and external stakeholders; builds consensus on complex, sensitive policy and technical matters involving divergent equities, reciprocity, and information sharing. Drives the modernization of adjudicative processes through the responsible integration of data analytics, workflow automation, and case-management systems; defines technical business requirements and ensures strict compliance with financial, privacy, and internal control protocols (including FIAR). Directs workforce capability development, including competency modeling and training strategies, to support merit principles; administers and justifies the program budget, determining resource priorities and monitoring contracted support to execute enterprise initiatives.

Details.JobSummary: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is a Defense Agency of the Department of War (DoW) under the direction, authority, and control of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence & Security (USW (I&S)).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission Through vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. To learn more about DCSA's mission and vision, visit: https://www.dcsa.mil/About-Us/Careers/.
MajorDuties: The Director of Financial Management and Comptroller serves as DCSA's senior financial-management executive and principal financial adviser to the DCSA Director and senior leadership. The incumbent directs and oversees the Agency's end-to-end financial-management program, including budget formulation and execution, accounting, funds control, financial reporting, internal controls, audit remediation, cost management, financial systems, and Working Capital Fund operations. The position provides independent, objective financial advice concerning Agency strategy, resource allocation, mission affordability, and financial risk. This is a Defense Intelligence Senior Executive Service Tier 2 position. The incumbent exercises executive direction and oversight of an annual financial portfolio of approximately $3.0 billion, comprising approximately $1.9 billion in Defense Working Capital Fund activity and $1.1 billion in appropriated funding. The incumbent directs the formulation, justification, execution, accounting, funds control, financial reporting, and performance assessment of these resources and oversees Working Capital Fund rate development, cost recovery, revenue and expense forecasting, cash management, customer billing, and long-term financial sustainability. Exercise executive direction and oversight of an annual financial portfolio exceeding $3.0 billion, comprising approximately $1.9 billion in Defense Working Capital Fund activity and $1.1 billion in appropriated funding. Direct the formulation, justification, execution, accounting, funds control, financial reporting, and performance assessment of these resources. Direct the financial governance of DCSA Working Capital Fund operations, including rate and price development, full-cost recovery, cash and corpus management, revenue, cost, and workload forecasting, customer billing, cost transparency, and the long-term financial sustainability of DCSA's fee-for-service operations. Establish and oversee DCSA's enterprise cost-accounting and cost-management framework. Ensure the consistent identification, accumulation, allocation, and reporting of direct and indirect costs to support Working Capital Fund rates, reimbursable pricing, program and activity cost transparency, customer billing, managerial decision-making, auditability, and assessment of mission efficiency. Serve as the principal financial adviser to the DCSA Director and senior leadership on financial management, resource allocation, fiscal risk, affordability, and the financial implications of Agency strategy and operating decisions. Represent DCSA before Departmental oversight organizations, the Office of Management and Budget, congressional committees and staff, Intelligence Community partners, customers, and other federal organizations on budgetary and financial-management matters. Establish and maintain an effective internal-control environment; direct financial-statement audit support, audit remediation, improper-payment and fraud-risk activities, and corrective actions addressing material weaknesses and other financial-management deficiencies. Provide executive oversight of financial management systems, business processes, financial data governance, and system modernization, ensuring reliable, timely, and decision-useful financial and cost information. Lead and develop DCSA's financial-management workforce and establish functional standards, workforce-development priorities, succession plans, and accountability for financial-management performance across headquarters and field organizations. Ensure compliance with appropriations law, fiscal controls, funds-control requirements, applicable accounting standards, and Departmental and Intelligence Community financial-management policies. Establish policy, governance, and financial controls for DCSA reimbursable activities and agreements. Oversee the development, review, acceptance, execution, billing, collection, reconciliation, closeout, and financial reporting of reimbursable orders to ensure full-cost recovery, proper use of funds, accurate customer billing, and compliance with applicable fiscal and financial-management requirements. Provide executive financial oversight of interagency agreements and other intra-governmental transactions, including agreements under the Economy Act and other applicable statutory authorities. Ensure that agreements contain appropriate funding authority, bona fide-need and period-of-availability determinations, cost estimates, billing provisions, internal controls, reconciliations, and closeout requirements.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES. Resumes over the 2-page limit, will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ 1. Demonstrated knowledge of the DoW Standards of Conduct, the Uniform Code of Military Justice, Freedom of Information and Privacy Acts, the Inspector General Act, statutory and regulatory protections for whistleblowers, and DoW or government wide regulations that pertain to personal conduct, official travel, use of Government resources, and whistleblower protection. Demonstrated knowledge of the IG complaint and appeal process. TQ 2. Demonstrated knowledge of the functions, procedures, and interrelationships of other IG elements; and the organizational structure and reporting chains within the DoN OR DoW. TQ 3. Demonstrated knowledge of the DoN or DoW administrative investigative policies, processes and procedures. The incumbent must have a demonstrated understanding of the Naval investigative practices and the ability to analyze complaints to identify relevant issues by reviewing and weighing evidence, separating fact from opinion, and making sound conclusions. The incumbent must have demonstrated ability to produce logical and technically accurate written products in plain language. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/senior-executive-service/

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as the Assistant Inspector General for Investigations in the Office of the Naval Inspector General (NAVINSGEN).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will direct the NAVINSGEN Investigations Division, including the DoW Hotline, Whistleblower Reprisal Investigations, and investigations involving senior officials.
You will develop and execute investigative policy, strategic objectives, and long-range goals aligned with the NAVINSGEN mission.
You will serve as liaison to the DoW Office of Inspector General and ensure effective Department of the Navy implementation of hotline and military whistleblower reprisal programs.
You will lead Inspector General oversight and reform initiatives, establishing policy and procedures that improve timeliness, transparency, and due process in administrative investigations.
You will oversee investigative intake, merit and jurisdiction determinations, analyses, progress reports, and final products to ensure compliance with applicable standards.
You will manage division resources, budget formulation, organizational requirements, and acquisition and sustainment of information management systems and related technology.
You will improve investigative processes, case-management data quality, trend analysis, records management, and Freedom of Information Act and Privacy Act response actions.
Details.Evaluations: This recruitment will utilize the following technical assessment tools: Structured Resume Review and Structured Interview. Minimally Qualified: Candidates meeting the basic minimum experience requirements for the position. Only applicants placed in the Best Qualified category will be referred. Details.JobSummary: As the principal advisor to the Center Commander and staff on logistics and sustainment, this leader directs an elite, multi-functional workforce to deliver world-class Life Cycle Logistics capabilities. They establish policy, drive rapid sustainment, and oversee critical processes for the life cycle management of advanced weapon systems, ensuring daily operational success and mission-ready capabilities for the warfighter.
Details.SubAgencyName: Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: Director, Logistics and Deputy Director, Enterprise Product Support (EPS) is the principal authority and senior advisor to the Center Commander, PAEs, and high-level defense officials (including AFMC, HAF, and OSW) on all logistics, rapid sustainment, and weapon systems life cycle management. As the Director, collaborates with PAEs to guide workforce planning, recruitment, training, and career development for the Center's logistics management workforce. Establishes professional and technical standards, sets workforce priorities, support selection of key personnel, and guides intern and developmental activities through subordinate supervisors. Advances employee development, readiness, retention, and professional growth. Leads workshops, action groups, and senior-level forums addressing workforce accession, development, health, safety, and retention. Develops, collaborates, and implements solutions that integrate logistics workforce capabilities that enable integration across mission areas that radically accelerate and deliver warfighting capabilities at speed. Serves as the primary touchpoint for strategic logistics issues and directly negotiates with senior defense contractors and partner nations. The incumbent resolves highly complex, systemic management issues, conducts independent performance assessments on high-cost acquisition programs, and leads high-level boards to optimize product support at the lowest life cycle cost. Provides executive-level direction across AFLCMC, geographically separated units, and multiple Air Force bases. The Director ensures strict compliance with DoW, HAF, and AFMC policies, manages the Directorate's budget and equipment, and implements standardized, data-driven sustainment methods across the enterprise. Drives continuous process improvement initiatives across all sustainment and product support activities. By defining functional interfaces and utilizing advanced data analytics, the Director monitors enterprise performance metrics to ensure alignment with modernized techniques and strategic defense objectives.
